The graph above is a result of the reflection and translation of $y=\sqrt{x}.$ Identify the equation that generated the graph.

$y=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To obtain the given graph, we can perform the following transformations:

- Take the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}.$

- Reflect the graph in the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\sqrt{-x}.$

The result is the solid blue curve shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14238243/assets/30add2e841bb25faa97692ec22309482c9b18d8c55f878057978f0896f7420ea.png)

- Reflect the graph in the $x$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\sqrt{-x}.$

The result is the solid blue curve shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14238243/assets/0bab48c1fe5e6d1a0d90b1aae3c8cd123327d1b2e18ca8101e056726b76de002.png)

- Translate the result to the right by $1$ units to get the graph of $y=-\sqrt{-(x-1)}.$

- Translate the result up by $4$ units to get the graph of $y=-\sqrt{-(x-1)}+4.$

The result is the solid blue curve shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14238243/assets/572a818b9621f8cec26f815429ff6d6e2846686afa348c7ae5a767dbd42fd3f6.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is $y=-\sqrt{-(x-1)}+4.$
